record.original_question: Does there exist a polytope P whose monodromy group Mon(P) is not a string C-group but that still has a unique minimal regular polytopal cover, or can one prove that no such polytope exists?

evidence.quote: Problem 5. Find a polytope P such that Mon(P) is not a string C-group, but P does have a unique minimal regular polytopal cover; or show the non-existence of such a polytope.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. An abstract polytope of rank n is a partially ordered set P with a strict rank function taking values in {-1, 0, …, n}, possessing a unique minimum element F_{-1} and unique maximum element F_n, in which every maximal chain (flag) has exactly n+2 elements, which is strongly flag-connected, and which satisfies the diamond condition: whenever F < G with rank(G) = rank(F)+2, there are exactly two elements H with F < H < G. The set of flags of P is denoted F(P). For each i ∈ {0,…,n-1} and each flag Φ ∈ F(P), there is a unique flag Φ^i differing from Φ only in its rank-i element; this defines an involution r_i on F(P).

The monodromy group Mon(P) is the subgroup of the symmetric group on F(P) generated by r_0, r_1, …, r_{n-1}.

A string C-group of rank n is a group G generated by involutions ρ_0,…,ρ_{n-1} satisfying (i) the string condition (ρ_iρ_j)^2 = 1 whenever |i-j| ≥ 2, and (ii) the intersection condition: ⟨ρ_i : i ∈ I⟩ ∩ ⟨ρ_i : i ∈ J⟩ = ⟨ρ_i : i ∈ I ∩ J⟩ for all I, J ⊆ {0,…,n-1}. Abstract regular polytopes correspond bijectively to string C-groups via their automorphism groups acting on a base flag.

A regular cover of P is an abstract regular polytope R together with a rank- and adjacency-preserving surjection R → P (i.e., a covering of flag systems commuting with each r_i). A minimal regular cover of P is a regular cover that does not properly cover any other regular cover of P.

Problem. Determine whether there exists an abstract polytope P such that:
(a) the monodromy group Mon(P) is not a string C-group, and
(b) P nonetheless admits a unique minimal regular polytopal cover;
or, alternatively, prove that no such polytope P exists.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up a definitive resolution of this specific question. Related work (e.g., on chiral polytopes whose smallest regular cover is itself a polytope, and on minimal covers of prisms, antiprisms, and Archimedean tilings) addresses adjacent cases but does not appear to settle the existence/non-existence question for polytopes with non-string-C-group monodromy yet a unique minimal regular polytopal cover. Status appears to remain unresolved based on available sources.

status_evidence.title: Chiral polytopes whose smallest regular cover is a polytope
status_evidence.snippet: Studies when the smallest regular cover of a chiral polytope is itself a polytope, addressing related but distinct cases.
status_evidence.claim: Related work addresses smallest regular covers in special cases, not the general non-string-C-group monodromy question.

status_evidence.title: Monodromy group - Polytope Wiki
status_evidence.snippet: For abstract polytopes of rank 4 or higher, minimal covers are not, in general, unique, nor do the monodromy groups of these polytopes necessarily satisfy the intersection condition.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the relevance of the question in rank ≥ 4 but does not resolve it.
